html:
The Congo to Ocean railway runs about 500 kilometres from Brazzaville to the port of Pointe-Noire, and was built by forced labour between 1921 and 1934.

The French wanted a route to the sea that did not depend on the Belgian line on the other bank. Workers were rounded up across French Equatorial Africa, from as far as Chad, and put to work cutting through the Mayombe mountains. Thousands died of disease, hunger and accidents. The writers André Gide and Albert Londres exposed the cost, which shocked opinion in France.

The line created the port of Pointe-Noire and tied the coast to Brazzaville. It remains the main artery of the country, carrying goods and people, and its history fed the anger behind Matsouanism.
sum: The Congo to Ocean railway runs about 500 kilometres from Brazzaville to the port of Pointe-Noire, and was built by forced labour between 1921 and 1934.
